svg.text: PHP 8.0, no framework. Boxes are what the code really is: page handlers, the classes in app/models/, the function modules that stand in for classes, and the entities the row arrays represent.
Solid arrow with a filled diamond: composition. Open arrow: association. Dashed open arrow: uses (a call).
Domain entities (a row is an array, not an object)
Function modules: files of functions that stand where a class would. The first four are all config/core.php, split by the concern they serve.
copied on archive, then deleted here
a message the student may act on;
any other exception is a fault and
- COLUMNS : one list, used by both inserts
+ document_name : string // the student's own name
+ the same column list as ResearchPaper
the helpers drawn on each entity

Not every page goes through a service. faculty_review_dashboard.php calls add_workflow() and set_status() itself and sets pending_admin, where admin_review_dashboard.php goes through PaperService; and faculty_manage_students.php
writes its own INSERT rather than using FacultyManagementService. That is the state of the code, not a simplification here.

No ORM and no entity classes: every row is an associative array from mysqli, and the operations drawn on an entity are free functions in config/core.php that take that array. The entity boxes are therefore the conceptual model the arrays stand for, which
is what the ERD declares as tables.
